text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of discrimination; municipal selection committees are typically assembled based on administrative roles, department heads, and HR representatives. 

For a director-level role, hiring decisions frequently weigh interview performance, leadership style, stakeholder management, and public consultation experience over paper credentials such as degrees and years of service. Alleging bias solely because the panel and selected candidate were women is legally groundless and could severely damage your professional reputation within municipal networks. 

A two-week wait for municipal administrative feedback is also entirely normal. Instead of raising gender, follow up politely to request constructive feedback on which competencies the panel prioritized.
